instruction: Change the font color of the title on slide 2 to black.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated to slide 2, selected the title text, opened font color picker and Character dialog, attempted to change color but set to Dark Gray 3 instead of black. Then moved to slide 3 and slide 4. Spent 50 turns without completing the multi-step task.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate between slides in LibreOffice Impress, select text in title shapes, open font color picker and Character dialog, interact with text boxes
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed to set the correct black color (chose Dark Gray 3 instead), could not bold titles correctly, and could not delete shapes/icons on slide 4. The original task was too complex with 3 sub-tasks across multiple slides.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a single font color change on one slide. The model demonstrated ability to navigate to the slide and open font color picker, so a focused single-color task should be achievable.
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing the title font color on slide 2 to black. Getter extracts the font color of the largest-font text shape on slide 2 (0-based index 1). Metric checks if the color equals '000000' (black).

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly targets slide 2 (0-based index 1) and extracts font color from the title shape identified by largest font size heuristic.
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' — directly accesses expected.get('expected_color') without incorrectly nesting into 'rules'.
Expected color '000000' correctly represents black, matching the instruction.
Postconfig properly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before evaluation to ensure state is persisted.

Minor issue: Only first_color (first run) is checked. If the title contains multiple runs, subsequent runs' colors are not verified. The instruction says to change the entire title's font color, so ideally all runs should be checked.

Minor issue: If font color is set via theme/inherited color rather than explicit RGB, run.font.color.rgb may be None, causing a false negative. However, an explicit user action to set black should typically set an explicit RGB value.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider checking all font colors in the title (not just first_color) to ensure the entire title text is black. The getter already extracts all colors in 'font_colors' — the metric could verify all non-None colors match the expected color.
Consider handling the case where font.color.rgb is None but the font.color.theme_color indicates black (e.g., theme color MSO_THEME_COLOR.TEXT_1 which is typically black).
